nodes.name: Big bluestem
nodes.desc: A tall native grass of the wet-meadow and prairie grasslands beside the river, and one of the plants Wikipedia lists along the Platte.

nodes.name: Plains cottonwood
nodes.desc: Cottonwood trees line the riverbanks and form part of the green oasis the Platte makes across semi-arid Nebraska.

nodes.name: Waste corn
nodes.desc: Leftover grain in harvested fields. Wikipedia notes it helps sandhill cranes build body reserves before they continue north.

nodes.name: Common Milkweed
nodes.desc: A common prairie wildflower of ditches and meadows here, and the plant monarch caterpillars feed on.

nodes.name: Cattail
nodes.desc: Tall marsh plants of shallow backwaters and wet meadows, eaten and used for lodges by muskrats.

nodes.name: Sandhill crane
nodes.desc: Up to 450,000 lesser sandhill cranes stop in the central Platte valley each year. They feed on waste grain, seeds and invertebrates in fields and wet meadows.

nodes.name: Snow goose
nodes.desc: Large flocks of migrating geese feed in the same harvested fields as the cranes and roost on the river.

nodes.name: Canada goose
nodes.desc: Wikipedia notes Canada geese have adapted to farm fields along the Platte, where they graze on grass and grain.

nodes.name: Mallard
nodes.desc: An omnivorous dabbling duck of shallow channels and backwaters, taking seeds, plants and small invertebrates.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: Wikipedia lists it among the Platte valley wildlife. It browses riverside trees and shrubs and eats grain and grasses.

nodes.name: Monarch butterfly
nodes.desc: The most-recorded insect in the area. Its caterpillars feed only on milkweed, and the adults pass through on migration.

nodes.name: Meadow vole
nodes.desc: A small grassland rodent that eats grasses and seeds and is prey for hawks, coyotes and snakes.

nodes.name: Muskrat
nodes.desc: A wetland rodent that eats cattails and other marsh plants and is hunted by many predators.

nodes.name: Raccoon
nodes.desc: An omnivore of the river corridor. It takes eggs, birds and small mammals, and is a recognised nest predator of cranes.

nodes.name: Bullsnake
nodes.desc: A large grassland snake that eats rodents and other small animals.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A common raptor of open country that hunts small mammals, birds and snakes.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: Wikipedia lists it among the Platte valley wildlife. It hunts waterfowl and can take adult cranes, and also scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A widespread predator that eats rodents, birds, fawns and carrion; it can take crane eggs and chicks.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives growth of the grasses, crops and marsh plants in the valley.

nodes.name: Platte River flow
nodes.desc: Spring and summer flows keep channels open and wet meadows green, but Wikipedia says river water is overappropriated and has shrunk since the mid-20th century.

nodes.name: Braided channels & sandbars
nodes.desc: The broad, shallow, braided river with shifting sandbars is the open roosting habitat cranes use at night.

nodes.name: River-valley soil
nodes.desc: Sandy, nutrient-rich floodplain soil under the meadows, fields and cottonwood groves.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass, leaves, grain, and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
